newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's foreign loan drawdown hits $442 mln in Q1.
newsitem.headline: Manila's foreign loan drawdown hits $442 mln in Q1.

text.p: The Philippine government has drawn $441.9 million of foreign loans in the first quarter of the year, up from $440.4 million it drew from foreign lenders in the same period last year, a government statement said on Tuesday.

The Asian Development Bank disbursed $102.7 million to the government during the quarter, up from $47.1 million released in the same period last year, the Coordinating Council of the Philippine Assistance Programme (CCPAP) said.
The World Bank released $56.6 million during the three-month period as against last year's $111.1 million, it said.
Japan's Overseas Economic Cooperation Fund disbursed 27.9 billion yen ($236 million) from 26.7 billion yen.
A total of $10.4 billion worth of loans has been pledged so far foreign governments and multilateral institutions to the Philippines to finance 154 projects, CCPAP said.
Manila has drawn $4.88 billion of that amount, it added.
